cards.back: To cause something to continue at the same level or rate. Example: 'It is important to maintain a healthy diet while preparing for exams.'
Important, serious, or significant in size or effect. Example: 'Unemployment is a major problem in many developing countries.'
The greater number or part of something; more than half. Example: 'The majority of students surveyed preferred online learning over traditional lectures.'
A particular way of doing something, especially a systematic or established one. Example: 'The researchers used a qualitative method to gather data from participants.'
Lesser in importance, seriousness, or significance. Example: 'The report contained a few minor errors that did not affect the overall findings.'
To observe and check the progress or quality of something over time. Example: 'Teachers monitor student attendance to identify those at risk of falling behind.'
To make something ineffective or to deny the existence of something. Example: 'Poor time management can negate the benefits of even the best study strategies.'
A group of interconnected people or things. Example: 'Building a professional network is essential for career development after graduation.'
Conforming to a standard; usual, typical, or expected. Example: 'It is normal for students to feel anxious before an important examination.'
A general understanding or idea about something. Example: 'The notion that technology always improves education is not supported by all research.'
To get or acquire something. Example: 'Students must obtain a minimum score of 6.5 to be admitted to the program.'
Easily perceived or understood; clear and apparent. Example: 'The obvious solution to traffic congestion is to invest more in public transportation.'
To fill or take up a space, time, or position. Example: 'Studying and part-time work occupy most of a typical student's day.'
To happen or take place. Example: 'Natural disasters occur more frequently in certain geographical regions.'
The result or effect of an action, situation, or event. Example: 'The outcome of the election will have a significant effect on education policy.'
Taking everything into account; general or comprehensive. Example: 'The overall quality of education has improved in most countries over the past two decades.'
To take part or become involved in an activity. Example: 'All students are encouraged to participate in class discussions to improve their speaking skills.'
A person or organization that takes part in an undertaking with another. Example: 'The university has formed a partnership with several industry partners to offer internships.'
One part in every hundred; a proportion expressed as a fraction of one hundred. Example: 'Approximately sixty percent of the population now has access to the internet.'
A length or portion of time. Example: 'The study was conducted over a period of three years.'
To allow someone to do something or to make something possible. Example: 'The new regulations do not permit smoking in any public building.'
A distinct stage in a process of change or development. Example: 'The project is currently in its initial phase of data collection.'
The study of fundamental questions about existence, knowledge, and values. Example: 'The philosophy of education explores how people learn and how teaching should be conducted.'
Relating to the body or to things that can be seen and touched. Example: 'Regular physical activity is recommended for maintaining good health.'
A course of action adopted and pursued by a government, organization, or individual. Example: 'The government introduced a new policy to reduce carbon emissions by thirty percent.'
Expressing agreement, approval, or a good or constructive quality. Example: 'The feedback from the pilot program was overwhelmingly positive.'
Having the capacity to develop into something in the future. Example: 'Renewable energy has the potential to replace fossil fuels within the next few decades.'
Existing or occurring before in time or order. Example: 'Previous research on this topic has produced conflicting results.'
Of chief importance; first in order of priority. Example: 'The primary goal of the program is to improve literacy rates among young children.'
A fundamental truth or rule that serves as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior. Example: 'The principle of equal opportunity is central to modern education systems.'
To begin or continue a course of action. Example: 'Once the application is approved, students may proceed with their enrollment.'
A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end. Example: 'The admissions process involves submitting academic transcripts and a personal statement.'
Relating to or connected with a profession, or showing a high standard of competence. Example: 'Professional development courses help teachers improve their classroom skills.'
A part, share, or number considered in relation to a whole. Example: 'A growing proportion of the workforce now works remotely from home.'
To make information available to the public, especially in printed or digital form. Example: 'The journal publishes articles on topics related to environmental science.'
To buy something. Example: 'Students can purchase textbooks online at a lower price than in campus bookshops.'
The extent or variety of different things within a given category. Example: 'The university offers a wide range of courses in the humanities and sciences.'
To respond or behave in a particular way in response to something. Example: 'People react differently to stressful situations depending on their personality.'
An area of a country or the world having definable characteristics. Example: 'The coastal region receives more rainfall than the interior of the country.'
To enter one's name on an official list or record. Example: 'Students must register for courses before the start of each semester.'
To control or supervise something by means of rules or laws. Example: 'The government regulates the food industry to ensure public safety.'
Closely connected or appropriate to what is being discussed or considered. Example: 'Only include information that is relevant to the essay question you are answering.'
To depend on with full trust or confidence. Example: 'Many students rely on scholarships to fund their university education.'
To take something away from a place or position. Example: 'The editor suggested removing unnecessary paragraphs to improve the essay's clarity.'
To need something or to make something necessary. Example: 'Most postgraduate programs require applicants to have a minimum IELTS score of 6.5.'
The systematic investigation and study of materials and sources to establish facts. Example: 'Further research is needed to understand the long-term effects of social media on young people.'
To live in a particular place. Example: 'A large number of international students reside in on-campus accommodation.'
A stock or supply of something that can be drawn on when needed. Example: 'Natural resources such as water and minerals must be managed sustainably.'
To say or act in reply to something. Example: 'The government responded to the crisis by providing emergency funding to affected communities.'
To put a limit on or keep under control. Example: 'Some countries restrict the amount of sugar allowed in food products sold to children.'
Income, especially that which a government or company receives regularly. Example: 'Tourism generates significant revenue for countries with popular holiday destinations.'
The function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation. Example: 'Teachers play a crucial role in shaping the attitudes and values of young people.'
Any of the more or less distinct parts into which something is divided. Example: 'The reading section of the IELTS exam lasts sixty minutes.'
A distinct part of the economy, society, or sphere of activity. Example: 'The technology sector has experienced rapid growth in the past decade.'
To carefully choose someone or something as being the best or most suitable. Example: 'Candidates are selected based on their qualifications and interview performance.'
Sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention. Example: 'There has been a significant improvement in air quality since the new regulations were introduced.'
Resembling something without being identical. Example: 'The education systems in these two countries are similar in many respects.'
A place, person, or thing from which something originates or can be obtained. Example: 'Academic journals are considered a reliable source of information for research papers.'
Clearly defined or identified; precise and detailed. Example: 'The assignment requires students to answer specific questions about the reading material.'
A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim. Example: 'Developing a clear study strategy can significantly improve exam results.'
The arrangement of and relations between the parts of something complex. Example: 'A well-organized essay follows a clear structure with an introduction, body, and conclusion.'
Enough to meet the needs of a situation or purpose. Example: 'Students must provide sufficient evidence to support their arguments in academic essays.'
An investigation of the opinions or experience of a group of people, based on a series of questions. Example: 'A recent survey found that most employees prefer flexible working arrangements.'
A piece of work to be done or undertaken. Example: 'Writing Task 2 of the IELTS exam requires candidates to write a discursive essay.'
A particular way of carrying out a task, especially involving practical skills. Example: 'Learning effective note-taking techniques can help students retain more information.'
The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry. Example: 'Advances in technology have transformed the way people access information.'
A set of principles on which an activity or subject is based. Example: 'Darwin's theory of evolution changed the way scientists understand biological development.'
A matter dealt with in a text, discussion, or conversation. Example: 'The topic of the lecture was the impact of globalization on local cultures.'
A custom or belief passed down through generations. Example: 'Many cultural traditions are being lost as societies become more modernized.'
To move from one place, person, or situation to another. Example: 'She decided to transfer to a different university to study marine biology.'
A system or means of carrying passengers or goods from one place to another. Example: 'Efficient public transport reduces traffic congestion and air pollution in cities.'
A general direction in which something is developing or changing. Example: 'There is a growing trend toward online education in higher learning institutions.'
Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else. Example: 'Each culture has unique traditions that distinguish it from others.'
Having a sound basis in logic or fact; reasonable or acceptable. Example: 'A valid argument must be supported by credible evidence and clear reasoning.'
To differ in size, amount, degree, or nature from something else. Example: 'Tuition fees vary considerably between public and private universities.'
